name: Joseph Goebbels
role: Nazi Gauleiter of Berlin and Reich Minister of Propaganda (1933-1945)
summary: Goebbels was a leading Nazi propagandist who, after an early period close to the party's Strasser wing, became a loyal follower of Hitler. His mature positions combine a one-party, leader-centred authoritarian state, extreme racial nationalism and violent antisemitism, hostility to liberalism, democracy and communism, and total mobilisation of society for war. He controlled press, radio, film and the arts and called for a 'people's community' in which class conflict gave way to national duty.

notes: Pass 3 (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-18) brings the audit to rules 7. Sources read: the complete Calvin/German Propaganda Archive collection of Goebbels' translated speeches and articles (the b2 compilation PDF, plus its separate pages), the 1933 Reich Chamber of Culture law, the USHMM articles on the book burning, Kristallnacht and the April 1933 boycott, and the Nuremberg transcript of 18 December 1945. Mature (1933-1945) positions are used; his early Strasserite anti-capitalist writings (1925-27) are not used for economic answers. Words are treated as his public positions; speeches were propaganda. Answers that rested on Wikipedia, on general values or on inference were nulled with the earlier version kept in reviewHistory. Themes searched for new answers: women and work, law and punishment, the press and radio, Jews and minorities, foreigners, the war and civilians, the church, property, labour and capital, the state, democracy, and foreign policy. Not read: the novel Michael and the diaries (no accessible text; see notFound), so views known only from the diaries stay null.
